title: Little Office of the Holy Cross

introductoryNotes.text: From a book of the same name published in 1800.
Non dicitur Alleluia, nec Laus tibi Domine.
introductoryNotes.english: Neither Alleluia nor Praise be to Thee, O Lord, is said.

translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: ℣. Per signum Crucis de inimicis nostris:
blocks.english: ℣. By the sign of the Cross, from our enemies:

blocks.source: ℟. Libera nos Deus noster. Ita dicitur in principio horarum.
blocks.english: ℟. Deliver us, O our God. Thus it is said at the beginning of the hours.

blocks.source: Domine labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

blocks.source: Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto, Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

blocks.source: Non dicitur Alleluia, nec Laus tibi Domine.
blocks.english: Neither Alleluia nor Praise be to Thee, O Lord, is said.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Patris sapientia, veritas divina: Deus homo captus est hora matutina. A notis discipulis cito derelictus: A Judaeis traditus, venditus, et afflictus.
blocks.english:
The Wisdom of the Father, the divine Truth,
God made man was taken captive at the hour of Matins.
Quickly deserted by His familiar disciples,
He was handed over by the Jews, sold, and afflicted.

blocks.source: Antiph. O Crux venerabilis, quae salutem attulisti miseris: quibus te efferam praeconis, quoniam vitam nobis caelestem praeparasti?
blocks.english: Ant. O venerable Cross, who hast brought salvation to the wretched: with what praises shall I extol thee, since thou hast prepared heavenly life for us?

blocks.source: ℣. Adoramus te Christe, et benedicimus tibi.
blocks.english: ℣. We adore Thee, O Christ, and we bless Thee.

blocks.source: ℟. Quia per sanctam Crucem tuam redemisti mundum.
blocks.english: ℟. Because by Thy holy Cross Thou hast redeemed the world.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe, Fili Dei vivi, pone Passionem, Crucem, et mortem tuam inter judicium tuum, et animam meam, nunc, et in hora mortis meae: et mihi largiri digneris gratiam et misericordiam: vivis et defunctis requiem et veniam: Ecclesiae tuae pacem et concordiam et nobis peccatoribus vitam et gloriam sempiternam. Qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, place Thy Passion, Cross, and death between Thy judgment and my soul, now and at the hour of my death: and vouchsafe to bestow upon me grace and mercy; upon the living and the departed, rest and pardon; upon Thy Church, peace and concord; and upon us sinners, life and everlasting glory. Who livest and reignest for ever and ever. Amen.

blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Hora prima Dominum ducunt ad Pilatum, Et a falsis testibus multum accusatum: Colaphis percutiunt, manibus ligatum: Vultum Dei conspuunt, lumen caeli gratum.
blocks.english:
At the first hour they lead the Lord to Pilate,
Accused at length by false witnesses.
They strike Him with blows, His hands bound;
They spit upon the face of God, the gracious light of heaven.

blocks.source: Antiph. O Crucis victoria, et admirabile signum: in caelesti curia fac nos captare triumphum.
blocks.english: Ant. O victory of the Cross and wondrous sign: make us attain triumph in the heavenly court.

blocks.source: Crucifige, crucifige, clamitat hora tertiam: Illusus induitur veste purpuram: Caput ejus pungitur corona spinarum: Crucem portat humeris ad locum poenarum.
blocks.english:
“Crucify, crucify!” they cry at the third hour.
Mocked, He is clothed in a purple garment.
His head is pierced by a crown of thorns;
He bears the Cross upon His shoulders to the place of punishment.

blocks.source: Antiph. Funestae mortis damnatur supplicium, dum Christus in Cruce nostra destruxit vincula criminum.
blocks.english: Ant. The punishment of grievous death is condemned, while Christ upon the Cross destroyed the bonds of our sins.

blocks.source: Hora sexta Jesus est Cruci conclavatus. Et cum latronibus pendens est deputatus: Prae tormentis sitiens felle saturatus: Agnus crimen diluens, sic est ludificatus.
blocks.english:
At the sixth hour Jesus is nailed to the Cross,
And, hanging there, is reckoned among thieves.
Thirsting amid His torments, He is given gall;
Thus is the Lamb, who washes away sin, mocked.

blocks.source: Antiph. Per lignum servi facti sumus, et per sanctam Crucem liberati sumus: fructus arboris seduxit nos: Filius Dei redemit nos.
blocks.english: Ant. Through a tree we became slaves, and through the holy Cross we were set free: the fruit of a tree deceived us; the Son of God redeemed us.

blocks.source: Hora nona Dominus Jesus expiravit: Eli clamans spiritum Patri commendavit: Latus ejus lancea miles perforavit: Terra tunc contremuit, et sol se obscuravit.
blocks.english:
At the ninth hour the Lord Jesus breathed His last.
Crying “Eli”, He commended His spirit to the Father.
A soldier pierced His side with a lance;
Then the earth trembled and the sun grew dark.

blocks.source: Antiph. O magnum pietatis opus! mors mortua tunc est, in ligno, quando mortua vita fuit.
blocks.english: Ant. O great work of loving mercy! Death itself died then upon the tree, when Life died.

blocks.source: De Cruce deponitur hora vespertina: Fortitudo latuit in mente divina: Talem mortem subiit vitae medicina: Heu corona gloriae jacuit supina!
blocks.english:
At the evening hour He is taken down from the Cross.
Strength lay hidden in the divine mind.
The remedy of life underwent such a death;
Alas, the crown of glory lay prostrate!

blocks.source: Antiph. O Crux benedicta, quae sola fuisti digna portare talentum mundi; dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulcia ferens pondera: super omnia ligna cedrorum tu sola excelsior, in qua mundi salus pependit; in qua Christus triumphavit, et mors mortem superavit in aeternum.
blocks.english: Ant. O blessed Cross, who alone wast worthy to bear the ransom of the world; sweet wood, sweet nails, bearing sweet burdens: thou alone art higher than all the cedar trees, upon whom the salvation of the world hung; upon whom Christ triumphed, and death overcame death for ever.

blocks.english: ℣. We adore Thee, O Christ, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Convertere nos Deus salutaris noster.
blocks.english: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Hora Completorii datur sepulturae Corpus Christi nobile, spes vitae futurae: Conduntur aromate: complentur Scripturae. Jugis sit memoria mortis suae dura.
blocks.english:
At the hour of Compline is given to burial
The noble body of Christ, the hope of future life.
It is laid away with spices; the Scriptures are fulfilled.
May the memory of His bitter death be unceasing.
blocks.editorialNote: The final Latin word is printed “dura”, retained here; the prepared English understands the phrase as referring to His bitter death.

blocks.source: Antiph. Salvator mundi salva nos, qui per Crucem, et sanguinem tuum redemisti nos; auxiliare nobis, te deprecamur, Deus noster.
blocks.english: Ant. Saviour of the world, save us, who by Thy Cross and blood hast redeemed us; help us, we beseech Thee, O our God.

blocks.source: ℣. Adoramus te Christe, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. We adore Thee, O Christ, etc.

Who livest and reignest for ever and ever. Amen.

blocks.source: Has Horas canonicas cum devotione. Tibi, Christe, recolo pia ratione: Ut qui pro me passus es amoris ardore, Sis mihi solatium mortis in agone. Amen.
blocks.english:
These canonical hours I devoutly recall
To Thee, O Christ, with loving reverence:
That Thou, who didst suffer for me with burning love,
Mayest be my consolation in the agony of death. Amen.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Vexilla Regis prodeunt: Fulget Crucis mysterium, Qua vita mortem pertulit, Et morte vitam protulit.
blocks.english:
The banners of the King go forth;
The mystery of the Cross shines brightly,
Upon which Life endured death,
And by death brought forth life.

blocks.source: Quae vulnerata lanceae Mucrone diro, criminum Ut nos lavaret sordibus, Manavit unda, et sanguine.
blocks.english:
Pierced by the cruel point of a lance,
That He might wash us from the stains of sin,
He poured forth water and blood.

blocks.source: Impleta sunt quae concinit David fideli carmine; Dicendo nationibus: Regnavit a ligno Deus.
blocks.english:
Fulfilled are the things that David sang
In faithful song,
Saying to the nations:
“God hath reigned from the tree.”

blocks.source: Arbor decora, et fulgida, Ornata Regis purpura, Electa digno stipite Tam sancta membra tangere.
blocks.english:
O fair and shining tree,
Adorned with the purple of the King,
Chosen, with worthy trunk,
To touch such holy limbs.

blocks.source: Beata, cujus brachiis Pretium pependit saeculi, Statera facta corporis Tulitque praedam tartari.
blocks.english:
Blessed tree, upon whose arms
Hung the ransom of the world;
Made the balance for His body,
Thou didst bear away the spoils of hell.

blocks.source: O Crux ave spes unica, Hoc passionis tempore, Piis adauge gratiam, Reisque dele crimina.
blocks.english:
Hail, O Cross, our only hope,
In this season of the Passion;
Increase grace for the devout,
And blot out the sins of the guilty.

blocks.source: Te, fons salutis, Trinitas: Collaudet omnis spiritus: Quibus Crucis victoriam Largiris, adde praemium.
blocks.english:
May every spirit praise Thee together,
O Trinity, fountain of salvation;
To those on whom Thou bestowest the victory of the Cross,
Add the reward.

blocks.source: Amen.
blocks.english: Amen.

blocks.source: Temp. Pasch. dic. Paschale quae fers gaudium. Per annum dic. In hac triumphii gloria.
blocks.english: In Eastertide say: “Who dost bear Paschal joy.” Throughout the year say: “In this glory of triumph.”

blocks.source: Oremus, Respice, quaesumus Domine, super hanc familiam tuam, pro qua Dominus noster Jesus Christus non dubitavit manibus tradi nocentium, et crucis subire tormentum. Qui tecum vivit, et regnat in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: Let us pray. Look, we beseech Thee, O Lord, upon this Thy family, for whom our Lord Jesus Christ did not hesitate to be delivered into the hands of the wicked and to undergo the torment of the Cross. Who liveth and reigneth with Thee for ever and ever. Amen.

editorialNotes.text: All four pages have been visually compared. English is prepared from the printed Latin. Abbreviated opening versicles, the Glory be, and Adoramus display the complete prayers printed in this office. The source gives no Lauds. The seasonal substitutions printed below Vexilla Regis apply to its “Hoc passionis tempore” line and are retained as instructions.
